title: First Unique Character in a String
statement: Return the index of the first character in `s` that appears exactly once. Return -1 when every character repeats.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: A second pass returns the first index whose count is 1.
One pass is not enough unless you also store indices, because you do not yet know whether a character will repeat.

approaches.name: Count then scan the string again
Index map
approaches.explanation: Store the first index and mark repeats as -1.

editorial: Count every character, then walk the string in order and return the first index whose count is one. The second walk is what preserves 'first'. A heap or sort would destroy that order.

examples.explanation: v is the first unique character.
